newsitem.title: UK: Shell up as Hoare Govett repeats "buy".
newsitem.headline: Shell up as Hoare Govett repeats "buy".

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport & Trading Co led oil stocks higher on Friday as analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett repeated a "buy" rating on the stock and the sector was boosted by renewed Iraq tensions, traders said.
Shell was up 6-1/2p at 991-1/2 by 0853 GMT in active trade of 1.8 million shares -- near its record 995p set September 17 -- and BP was up 4-1/2p at 650-1/2.

Traders said Hoare Govett analysts had repeated their positive stance on Shell after a meeting with company executives yesterday, but analysts at the brokerage declined comment on their discussions with the company.
Meantime, renewed U.S. military activity around Iraq renewed hopes for higher oil prices, traders said.

U.S. ground troops were yesterday deployed in Kuwait under orders to head into the desert with battle tanks close to the Iraqi border, while aircraft carrier USS Enterprise also arrived as part of a huge U.S. military build-up.
"We have another aircraft carrier heading into the gulf and that is not going to do any harm to oil prices," said one trader.
Crude prices have dipped in the past week but still stand well above their levels at the end of July. Brent crude closed yesterday at $22.08 a barrel compared with $19.00 on July 31.
Elsewhere in the oil sector Enterprise Oil Plc was up 4p at 522-1/2.
